Let's produce solution with reasoning step by step, showing algebraic simplification. Also discuss handling of angle reductions. Provide final answer.<|end_think|>\[
\frac{\cot2006-1}{\csc2006-\sec2006}
\]

Write everything in terms of \(\sin\) and \(\cos\).

\[
\cot\theta=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta},\qquad 
\csc\theta=\frac1{\sin\theta},\qquad 
\sec\theta=\frac1{\cos\theta}
\qquad(\theta=2006^\circ)
\]

Hence  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{numerator}&=\cot\theta-1
                 =\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}-1
                 =\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta},\\[4pt]
\text{denominator}&=\csc\theta-\sec\theta
                 =\frac1{\sin\theta}-\frac1{\cos\theta}
                 =\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now divide the numerator by the denominator:

\[
\frac{\displaystyle\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta}}
     {\displaystyle\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}}
=
\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta}\,
\cdot\,
\frac{\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}
=\cos\theta .
\]

Thus the whole expression equals \(\cos 2006^\circ\).

Since the cosine function has period \(360^\circ\),

\[
\cos 2006^\circ=\cos\bigl(2006-5\cdot360\bigr)^\circ
            =\cos 206^\circ.
\]

Finally, \(206^\circ = 180^\circ+26^\circ\), and \(\cos(180^\circ+\alpha)=-\cos\alpha\). Hence

\[
\cos2006^\circ = \cos 206^\circ = -\cos 26^\circ .
\]

\[
\boxed{-\cos 26^\circ}
\] (equivalently \(\boxed{\cos2006^\circ}\)).<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
